newsitem.title: USA: U.S corporate bond market sees little issuance Fri.
newsitem.headline: U.S corporate bond market sees little issuance Fri.

text.p: U.S. corporate bond deals for investment-grade borrowers are expected to remain at a trickle today but corporate syndicate sources said the pace should pick up next week given the attractive low interest rates.
"I think we should see a pickup next week but I haven't heard anything specific yet," said one syndicate source at a U.S. investment firm.
A $1.25 billion global bond for Ford Motor Credit, which priced today, was the only deal expected. The 6-1/2 percent global bonds were priced at 99.916 to yield 38 basis points over U.S. Treasuries.
Ford Motor Credit, which is rated A-1 by Moody's Investors Service Inc and A-plus by Standard & Poor's Corp, was priced via lead managers Goldman Sachs and Salomon Brothers Inc.
In the high-yield area, three new issues totalling about $500 million may be priced later today, sources said.

Adelphia Communications Corp is expected to issue a 144a offering of at least $200 million in 10-year senior notes via Smith Barney. Price talk is for a coupon of 9-7/8 percent to 10 percent. The company said it will use the proceeds from the offering to redeem a portion of its 12-1/2 percent notes which become callable in May, as well as to pay down bank debt.
Among other new high-yield issues expected today were Packard Industries' $125 million 144A senior subordinated note offering due 2007 via lead manager Merrill Lynch.
Price talk on the deal is for a coupon of 9-3/8 percent to 9-1/2 percent. The issue is rated B-3 by Moody's Investors Service and B-minus by Standard and Poor's Corp.
ALso, Diamond Cable Communications is expected to price $175 million 144A senior discount notes due 2007 via lead manager Goldman Sachs & Co. Price talk is 10-3/4 to 10-7/8 percent.

Set for pricing Monday is Fonda Group's $110 million 144A senior subordinated note offering due 2007. Price talk on the deal, which is to be lead-managed by Bear Stearns, is for a coupon of 9-1/4 to 9-1/2 percent.
